July fourteenth, eighteen eighty-two. A teamster hauling wood up a mountain road in southeastern Arizona notices a man sitting against an oak tree, right beside the creek.
From a distance, he looks like he's resting. Two women had ridden past him the day before and thought exactly that.
He wasn't resting.

The biggest of those eruptions threw out more than a thousand times the material of the 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens. Searing clouds of ash and gas raced across the land and buried more than twelve hundred square miles.
